questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

No card is a picture.

Some pictures are frames.

No frame is a lens.

**Conclusions:**

I. No card is a frame.

II. All pictures can never be lenses.

III. At least some cards are lenses.

options.text: All conclusions I, II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

No card is a picture.

Some pictures are frames.

No frame is a lens.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6bfb9fd04767383ed364c3bf7e13e0566844195ebb5fe0a0ba0fbe828a9cd41.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No card is a frame - False (Because, No definite relation given between card and frame, so it can be possible only).

II. All pictures can never be lenses - True (Because, those part of pictures which is frames is definitely not lens, and all pictures can never be lenses will be true).

III. At least some cards are lenses - False (Because, No definite relation given between cards and lenses, so it can be possible only).

So, Only conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'HUT’ is coded as '55' and 'MAT' is coded as '40'. How will 'BIB' be coded in that language?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **(Sum of the place values of the alphabets) + 6**.

Now,

'HUT' is coded as '55'

⇒ H(8) + U(21) + T(20) + 6

⇒ 49 + 6 = 55.

'MAT' is coded as '40'

⇒ M(13) + A(1) + T(20) + 6

⇒ 34 + 6 = 40.

Similarly, for **‘BIB’ **

**⇒ B(2) + I(9) + B(2) + 6**

**⇒ 13 + 6 = 19.**

So, **'BIB' will be coded as '19'**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'DOUBLE' is coded as ‘59’, CHECK’ is coded as ‘30’. How will 'GLITTER' be coded in that language?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **Sum of the place values of the alphabets**.

Now,

‘DOUBLE’ is coded as ‘59’

⇒ D(4) + O(15) + U(21) + B(2) + L(12) + E(5) = 59.

‘CHECK’ is coded as ‘30’

⇒ C(3) + H(8) + E(5) + C(3) + K(11) = 30.

Similarly, for **‘GLITTER’ **

**⇒ G(7) + L(12) + I(9) + T(20) + T(20) + E(5) + R(18) = 91.**

So, **'GLITTER' will be coded as '91'**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some sounds are noises.

All noises are debates.

Some debates are conversations.

**Conclusions:**

I. No noise is a conversation.

II. At least some conversations are sounds.

III. Some sounds are debates.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

Some sounds are noises.

All noises are debates.

Some debates are conversations.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6f37547ee2e1cebab8ca5a863305010c39bd9355612ac867516b6681103f93e5.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No noise is a conversation - False (Because, No definite relation given between noise and conversation, so it can be possible only).

II. At least some conversations are sounds - False (Because, No definite relation given between conversations and sounds, so it can be possible only).

III. Some sounds are debates - True (Because, Some sounds are noises and All noises are debates gives some sounds are debates).

So, Only conclusion III follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
